contentStandardDescription: Describe numbers and the relationship between numbers 0 to 100
indicatorDescription: Use number names, counting sequences and how to count to find out 'how many?' (forwards/backwards by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s between 0 and 100).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and model the concept of: use number names, counting sequences and how to count to find out 'how many?' (forwards/backwards by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s between 0 and 100).
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Counters (bottle tops, stones); number cards 0–100; abacus; number chart; Pattern cards; colored beads; counting frames
keywords: number names, counting sequences, how to count, forwards, backwards, how many
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a fun number song like '1, 2, Buckle My Shoe' or 'Ten Green Bottles' with clapping.
Have pupils do a quick oral counting exercise from 1 to 20, first forwards and then backwards.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin learning about 1. number: counting, representation, cardinality & ordinality using real counters.'
Write today's key words on the board: 'number names' and read it aloud together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models. Displays concrete counters (stones, bottle caps) or ten-frames. Shows how to count, add, subtract or partition a whole group clearly.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Concrete Practice - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups. Teacher gives each group a bundle of counters and guides them to repeat the count, addition, or subtraction.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Discovery - 7 min): Groups solve simple concrete puzzles (e.g. making groups of 5, matching coins to values, or folding paper to show halves).
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher monitors groups, correcting hand placements on counters, and reinforcing mathematical vocabulary.
plenary: Whole class sings a joyful counting song together with body actions.
Ask: 'What did we learn to count or do today?' (Have 2-3 pupils explain).
Homework: 'Find 10 small objects at home (seeds, bottle caps) and count them to your parents.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson: we will write and draw our numbers!
assessment: Oral counting check; practical counting task; number-naming drill; missing number exercise

contentStandardDescription: Describe numbers and the relationship between numbers 0 to 100
indicatorDescription: Use number names, counting sequences and how to count to find out 'how many?' (forwards/backwards by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s between 0 and 100).
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to practice and represent: use number names, counting sequences and how to count to find out 'how many?' (forwards/backwards by 1s, 2s, 5s, and 10s between 0 and 100).
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Counters (bottle tops, stones); number cards 0–100; abacus; number chart; Pattern cards; colored beads; counting frames
keywords: number names, counting sequences, how to count, forwards, backwards, how many
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and play a quick game of 'Mental Math Buzz' where we count and clap on even numbers.
Review yesterday's work: ask 2-3 pupils to show a number of counters on their desk.
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to practice writing and representing our 1. number: counting, representation, cardinality & ordinality.'
Write the key words 'number names, counting sequences' on the board and pronounce them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Pictorial Practice - 5 min): Pupils draw circles in their books to match number cards or symbols (<, >, =). Teacher guides them to use place value and counting strategies.
ACTIVITY 3 (Individual Practice - 7 min): Pupils complete a series of simple pictorial math tasks in their notebooks (e.g., adding two groups, counting halves, writing missing numbers).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated number rhyme or does a mental math flash drill.
Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Oral counting check; practical counting task; number-naming drill; missing number exercise

contentStandardDescription: Recognize, create, extend and describe non-numerical and simple numerical patterns
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explore and solve tasks on: demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Analyse attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects to develop general concepts about their properties
indicatorDescription: Distinguish between attributes that define a two-dimensional figure or three-dimensional figure and attributes that do not.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explore and solve tasks on: distinguish between attributes that define a two-dimensional figure or three-dimensional figure and attributes that do not.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation; Cultural Identity
resources: Cut-outs of 2D shapes (circles, squares, triangles); 3D objects (balls, cans, boxes); sorting trays; attribute blocks
keywords: distinguish, attributes, defining attributes, sides, corners, face, non-defining attributes, size, color, orientation
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 1. 2d and 3d shapes.'
Write today's key term 'distinguish' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Practical shape sorting check; attribute matching worksheet; shape-naming quiz

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explore and solve tasks on: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

contentStandardDescription: Describe numbers and the relationship between numbers 0 to 100
indicatorDescription: Identify numbers in different positions around a given number (0 – 100) using a 100-number chart.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and model the concept of: identify numbers in different positions around a given number (0 – 100) using a 100-number chart.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Number cards 0–100; pocket chart; large 100-number wall chart; pointer; individual number charts
keywords: identify numbers, positions, before, after, between, number chart
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a fun number song like '1, 2, Buckle My Shoe' or 'Ten Green Bottles' with clapping.
Have pupils do a quick oral counting exercise from 1 to 20, first forwards and then backwards.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin learning about 1. number: counting, representation, cardinality & ordinality using real counters.'
Write today's key words on the board: 'identify numbers' and read it aloud together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models. Displays concrete counters (stones, bottle caps) or ten-frames. Shows how to count, add, subtract or partition a whole group clearly.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Concrete Practice - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups. Teacher gives each group a bundle of counters and guides them to repeat the count, addition, or subtraction.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Discovery - 7 min): Groups solve simple concrete puzzles (e.g. making groups of 5, matching coins to values, or folding paper to show halves).
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher monitors groups, correcting hand placements on counters, and reinforcing mathematical vocabulary.
plenary: Whole class sings a joyful counting song together with body actions.
Ask: 'What did we learn to count or do today?' (Have 2-3 pupils explain).
Homework: 'Find 10 small objects at home (seeds, bottle caps) and count them to your parents.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson: we will write and draw our numbers!
assessment: Oral identification check; fill-in-the-blanks chart; pointer drill

contentStandardDescription: Describe numbers and the relationship between numbers 0 to 100
indicatorDescription: Identify numbers in different positions around a given number (0 – 100) using a 100-number chart.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to practice and represent: identify numbers in different positions around a given number (0 – 100) using a 100-number chart.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Number cards 0–100; pocket chart; large 100-number wall chart; pointer; individual number charts
keywords: identify numbers, positions, before, after, between, number chart
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and play a quick game of 'Mental Math Buzz' where we count and clap on even numbers.
Review yesterday's work: ask 2-3 pupils to show a number of counters on their desk.
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to practice writing and representing our 1. number: counting, representation, cardinality & ordinality.'
Write the key words 'identify numbers, positions' on the board and pronounce them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Pictorial Practice - 5 min): Pupils draw circles in their books to match number cards or symbols (<, >, =). Teacher guides them to use place value and counting strategies.
ACTIVITY 3 (Individual Practice - 7 min): Pupils complete a series of simple pictorial math tasks in their notebooks (e.g., adding two groups, counting halves, writing missing numbers).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated number rhyme or does a mental math flash drill.
Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Oral identification check; fill-in-the-blanks chart; pointer drill

contentStandardDescription: Recognize, create, extend and describe non-numerical and simple numerical patterns
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Analyse attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects to develop general concepts about their properties
indicatorDescription: Distinguish between attributes that define a two-dimensional figure or three-dimensional figure and attributes that do not.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: distinguish between attributes that define a two-dimensional figure or three-dimensional figure and attributes that do not.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation; Cultural Identity
resources: Cut-outs of 2D shapes (circles, squares, triangles); 3D objects (balls, cans, boxes); sorting trays; attribute blocks
keywords: distinguish, attributes, defining attributes, sides, corners, face, non-defining attributes, size, color, orientation
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 1. 2d and 3d shapes.'
Write today's key term 'distinguish' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Practical shape sorting check; attribute matching worksheet; shape-naming quiz

NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 1. 2d and 3d shapes.'
Write today's key term 'distinguish' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Practical shape sorting check; attribute matching worksheet; shape-naming quiz

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

contentStandardDescription: Describe numbers and the relationship between numbers 0 to 100
indicatorDescription: Use number names and non-standard units for measuring (lengths and volumes) to count to find out 'how long or how much?' up to 100.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and model the concept of: use number names and non-standard units for measuring (lengths and volumes) to count to find out 'how long or how much?' up to 100.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Hand-spans, feet, paces, referent materials; plastic cups, spoons, water basin, sand; various small containers; counters
keywords: number names, non-standard units, length, volume, how long, how much
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a fun number song like '1, 2, Buckle My Shoe' or 'Ten Green Bottles' with clapping.
Have pupils do a quick oral counting exercise from 1 to 20, first forwards and then backwards.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin learning about 1. number: counting, representation, cardinality & ordinality using real counters.'
Write today's key words on the board: 'number names' and read it aloud together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models. Displays concrete counters (stones, bottle caps) or ten-frames. Shows how to count, add, subtract or partition a whole group clearly.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Concrete Practice - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups. Teacher gives each group a bundle of counters and guides them to repeat the count, addition, or subtraction.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Discovery - 7 min): Groups solve simple concrete puzzles (e.g. making groups of 5, matching coins to values, or folding paper to show halves).
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher monitors groups, correcting hand placements on counters, and reinforcing mathematical vocabulary.
plenary: Whole class sings a joyful counting song together with body actions.
Ask: 'What did we learn to count or do today?' (Have 2-3 pupils explain).
Homework: 'Find 10 small objects at home (seeds, bottle caps) and count them to your parents.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson: we will write and draw our numbers!
assessment: Practical measuring task; record-keeping sheet; oral Q&A on comparisons

contentStandardDescription: Describe numbers and the relationship between numbers 0 to 100
indicatorDescription: Use number names and non-standard units for measuring (lengths and volumes) to count to find out 'how long or how much?' up to 100.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to practice and represent: use number names and non-standard units for measuring (lengths and volumes) to count to find out 'how long or how much?' up to 100.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Hand-spans, feet, paces, referent materials; plastic cups, spoons, water basin, sand; various small containers; counters
keywords: number names, non-standard units, length, volume, how long, how much
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and play a quick game of 'Mental Math Buzz' where we count and clap on even numbers.
Review yesterday's work: ask 2-3 pupils to show a number of counters on their desk.
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to practice writing and representing our 1. number: counting, representation, cardinality & ordinality.'
Write the key words 'number names, non-standard units' on the board and pronounce them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Pictorial Practice - 5 min): Pupils draw circles in their books to match number cards or symbols (<, >, =). Teacher guides them to use place value and counting strategies.
ACTIVITY 3 (Individual Practice - 7 min): Pupils complete a series of simple pictorial math tasks in their notebooks (e.g., adding two groups, counting halves, writing missing numbers).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated number rhyme or does a mental math flash drill.
Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Practical measuring task; record-keeping sheet; oral Q&A on comparisons

contentStandardDescription: Recognize, create, extend and describe non-numerical and simple numerical patterns
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Recognize, create, extend and describe non-numerical and simple numerical patterns
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Analyse attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects to develop general concepts about their properties
indicatorDescription: Identify three-dimensional shapes, including spheres, cones, cylinders, rectangular prisms (including cubes), and triangular prisms, and describe their attributes.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: identify three-dimensional shapes, including spheres, cones, cylinders, rectangular prisms (including cubes), and triangular prisms, and describe their attributes.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation; Cultural Identity
resources: Spheres (balls), cones (ice-cream cones), cylinders (cans), rectangular prisms (boxes), cubes (dice), triangular prisms; multi-base blocks; hand lens
keywords: identify, 3D shapes, sphere, cone, cylinder, rectangular prism, cube, triangular prism, face, edge, vertex, vertices
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 1. 2d and 3d shapes.'
Write today's key term 'identify' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: 3D object identification; attribute description check; classroom shape hunt

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.

contentStandardDescription: Develop strategies for adding and subtracting within 20
indicatorDescription: Use strategies for solving basic addition facts (and related subtraction facts) to 10.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to practice and represent: use strategies for solving basic addition facts (and related subtraction facts) to 10.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Counters; number line; addition flashcards; subtraction flashcards; ten-frames; finger counting; double-sided counters
keywords: strategies, basic facts, addition, subtraction, doubles, near-doubles, make-ten
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand in a circle and play a quick game of 'Mental Math Buzz' where we count and clap on even numbers.
Review yesterday's work: ask 2-3 pupils to show a number of counters on their desk.
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to practice writing and representing our 2. number operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division).'
Write the key words 'strategies, basic facts' on the board and pronounce them.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Pictorial Practice - 5 min): Pupils draw circles in their books to match number cards or symbols (<, >, =). Teacher guides them to use place value and counting strategies.
ACTIVITY 3 (Individual Practice - 7 min): Pupils complete a series of simple pictorial math tasks in their notebooks (e.g., adding two groups, counting halves, writing missing numbers).
ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.
plenary: Whole class recites a consolidated number rhyme or does a mental math flash drill.
Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Mental math drill; rapid card flash exercise; practical strategy demonstration

contentStandardDescription: Recognize, create, extend and describe non-numerical and simple numerical patterns
indicatorDescription: Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns with 2 to 4 repeating elements.
competencies: Communication & Collaboration; Critical Thinking & Problem Solving
resources: Pattern cards; colored beads; colored blocks; fruit slices; pattern strips; musical clap patterns
keywords: patterns, repeating elements, extend, identify, create, core pattern, non-numerical, simple numerical
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.
Ask: 'What comes next in our clapping pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Practice - 5 min): Pupils use pattern cards and colored counters on their desks to duplicate and extend the teacher's pattern. Teacher checks their placements.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Creative Task - 7 min): In small groups, pupils create their own repeating patterns with 3 or 4 elements using seeds, bottle caps, or drawings. They explain their pattern to other groups.
ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

contentStandardDescription: Analyse attributes of two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects to develop general concepts about their properties
indicatorDescription: Identify two-dimensional shapes, including circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, rhombuses, and hexagons, and describe their attributes.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: identify two-dimensional shapes, including circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, rhombuses, and hexagons, and describe their attributes.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Creativity & Innovation; Cultural Identity
resources: Cut-outs of circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, rhombuses, hexagons; geoboards with rubber bands; shape stencils
keywords: identify, 2D shapes, circle, triangle, rectangle, square, rhombus, hexagon, sides, corners, vertices
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 1. 2d and 3d shapes.'
Write today's key term 'identify' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Geoboard shape-making test; 2D shape drawing check; matching sides & corners worksheet

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.

plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.

NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'

ACTIVITY 4 (Peer Review - 3 min): Groups walk around to view other tables' patterns, trying to identify and correct any errors. Teacher commends great peer sharing.
plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.
Ask: 'What is a pattern?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to describe in their own words).
Homework: 'Look for patterns in your home (on fabrics, mats, walls) and draw them in your notebook.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Geometry and Shapes.
assessment: Pattern-extending check; create-your-own-pattern task; matching card game

starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a body pattern clap: 'Clap, Clap, Stamp, Clap, Clap, Stamp.' Have pupils join in.

NEW TODAY: State the focus: 'Today we are going to create and extend beautiful patterns of shapes and numbers.'
Write the keyword 'patterns' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher uses colored blocks (or drawings) to create an ABAB repeating pattern: 'Red triangle, blue circle, red triangle, blue circle.' Demonstrates finding the core pattern.

plenary: Whole class does a fun clapping and stomping pattern together.

contentStandardDescription: Describe the position of objects in space
indicatorDescription: Tell the position of objects relative to other objects in space using positional words.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: tell the position of objects relative to other objects in space using positional words.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom furniture; toys; PE cones; positional picture cards; boxes and small toys
keywords: position of objects, relative, above, below, to the right, to the left, in front of, behind, next to
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners. Stand up and sing 'This is a circle, this is a square' to a popular local primary school tune.
Have pupils look around the room and point to one round object and one flat object.
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's focus: 'Today we are starting our study of 2. position and space.'
Write today's key term 'position of objects' on the board and read it together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher displays real 3D shapes (sphere, cylinder, cube) or 2D cut-outs (triangle, rectangle). Models describing attributes: 'This is a cube. It has flat faces and corners.'
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Exploration - 5 min): Pupils hold shape models, touch the edges, faces, and corners. For position/measurement, pupils follow instructions (e.g. 'Put the block behind your box').
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Sorting / Comparison - 7 min): Groups sort a mixture of 2D/3D shapes by attributes (defining vs. non-defining) or compare pairs of objects (longer/shorter, heavier/lighter).
ACTIVITY 4 (Reflection & Feedback - 3 min): Selected pupils stand up and describe their shape or comparison to the class: 'My pencil is longer than my crayon.' Teacher reinforces geometric terms.
plenary: Whole class sings today's shape song with physical movements.
Ask: 'What shape or position did we study today?' (Have 2-3 pupils describe).
Homework: 'Find two shapes or compare two objects in your kitchen and tell your parents which is bigger/longer.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson on Data and charts.
assessment: Follow-the-position instructions drill; relative position Q&A; classroom map sketch

subStrandName: Data Collection, Organisation, Interpretation, Presentation and Analysis
contentStandardDescription: Organise, represent and interpret data
indicatorDescription: Organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to review and demonstrate: organise and represent (using pictures/objects) data with up to three categories.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Personal Development & Leadership
resources: Classroom objects (pencils, books, water bottles); colored counters; tally sheets; large board chart; cut-out picture cards; pictograph grid
keywords: organise, represent, pictures, objects, data, three categories, pictograph, tally
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Ask pupils: 'How many boys are in the front row? Let's count them together.'
Show three different colored blocks and say: 'Let's see which color our class likes best!'
NEW TODAY: Introduce today's lesson: 'Today we are learning how to collect, organize and represent our own data.'
Write today's key word 'organise' on the board and read it aloud.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models gathering data. Asks 10 pupils their favorite fruit (mango, banana, orange). Writes tally marks on the blackboard and counts them.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Representation - 5 min): Teacher guides pupils to draw simple squares/circles to represent each vote in a neat pictograph on the board. Class counts the total data points.

ACTIVITY 3 (Group Data Collection - 7 min): In small groups, pupils collect data on their own (e.g., color of pencils, type of shoes) and organize it into a small pictograph using cut-out picture cards.
ACTIVITY 4 (Comparison Discussion - 3 min): Groups compare categories in their data (e.g., 'Most pencils are yellow, least are blue'). Teacher checks and validates their tallying and comparisons.
plenary: Whole class counts today's data charts and celebrates with a rhythmic clap.
Ask: 'Why do we collect data?' (Call on 2-3 pupils to share why charts are useful).
Homework: 'Ask 5 family members if they like tea or juice better. Tally their answers.'
Preview next week's exciting mathematics adventure.
assessment: Practical sorting and pictograph creation; class exercise; oral Q&A on data representation

contentStandardDescription: Understand the fraction one-half as a part of a whole
indicatorDescription: Understand the fraction one-half as the quantity obtained by taking 1 part when a whole is partitioned into two equal parts.
performanceIndicator: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify and model the concept of: understand the fraction one-half as the quantity obtained by taking 1 part when a whole is partitioned into two equal parts.
competencies: Critical Thinking & Problem Solving; Communication & Collaboration
resources: Paper sheets (circles, rectangles); real apples, oranges, or loaves of bread; safety plastic scissors; play dough; fraction bars
keywords: fraction, one-half, half, whole, equal parts, partition, divide
rpk: Learners have basic everyday experiences related to this mathematics topic.
starter: Greet learners warmly. Lead the class in a fun number song like '1, 2, Buckle My Shoe' or 'Ten Green Bottles' with clapping.
Have pupils do a quick oral counting exercise from 1 to 20, first forwards and then backwards.
NEW TODAY: State the lesson focus: 'Today we will begin learning about 3. fractions using real counters.'
Write today's key words on the board: 'fraction' and read it aloud together.
main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher models. Displays concrete counters (stones, bottle caps) or ten-frames. Shows how to count, add, subtract or partition a whole group clearly.
ACTIVITY 2 (Guided Concrete Practice - 5 min): Pupils work in small groups. Teacher gives each group a bundle of counters and guides them to repeat the count, addition, or subtraction.
ACTIVITY 3 (Group Discovery - 7 min): Groups solve simple concrete puzzles (e.g. making groups of 5, matching coins to values, or folding paper to show halves).
ACTIVITY 4 (Review - 3 min): Teacher monitors groups, correcting hand placements on counters, and reinforcing mathematical vocabulary.
plenary: Whole class sings a joyful counting song together with body actions.
Ask: 'What did we learn to count or do today?' (Have 2-3 pupils explain).
Homework: 'Find 10 small objects at home (seeds, bottle caps) and count them to your parents.'
Preview tomorrow's lesson: we will write and draw our numbers!
assessment: Practical paper-folding task; coloring half-shapes worksheet; oral identification of halves

main: ACTIVITY 1 (Modelling - 5 min): Teacher reviews yesterday's concrete concepts and shows how to represent them on the board using drawings (circles, tallies, number lines, symbols).

ACTIVITY 4 (Sharing & Discussion - 3 min): Selected pupils show their notebook drawings on the board. Class applauds, and teacher summarizes key math patterns.

Ask: 'Who can tell me what symbol or number we drew today?' (Call on 2-3 pupils).
Homework: 'Complete today's notebook drawing at home and show it to your family.'
Preview tomorrow's exciting lesson on Algebra and Patterns.
assessment: Practical paper-folding task; coloring half-shapes worksheet; oral identification of halves
